finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but ignores the boolean result (it should call assertCanDelete), so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id (broken access control / IDOR).
finding.source: Any authenticated user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) takes the attacker-controlled id from the route
Account a = accounts.get(id) fetches the victim's account
canDelete(u,a) is evaluated but its return value is discarded, so there is no throw and no early return

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (line 9-11) has correct logic but is not enforced here. assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is not called in this method. No other auth layer exists in the code. closeAccount (27-31) does enforce assertCanDelete, so it is not affected by this finding. A nonexistent id gives a null account and canDelete would NPE, but only after the missing check, which does not stop deletion.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean, but it's called as a bare statement at line 22 with the result discarded; assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but isn't called in deleteAccount. No other auth layer exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: AccountService.java:22 calls canDelete(u, a) and discards the boolean, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any user (closeAccount at line 29 correctly uses assertCanDelete).
